# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 59 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 59 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_059_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 59 provides the comprehensive allegorical key to the vineyard parable. The assignments are: field = world; lord of field = God; son = Holy Spirit; slave = Son of God; vine = the people; fences = guardian angels; weeds = transgressions; feast foods = commandments through the Son; friends/counselors = first-created angels; master's absence = remaining time before the parousia.

The identification of the "friends" as "holy prophets who served God" in 59:4 (slightly different from 59:2's "first-created angels" for "friends") suggests either different categories of "friends" in the parable, or textual confusion. Scholars note tension between the two identifications.

The rhetorical move in 59:3 — "could I have perceived these things?" / "anyone with God in their heart would not hesitate to ask" — is pastoral encouragement to inquire. Hermas is not naturally a mystic; he needs things explained. His self-deprecation here is part of his prophetic persona.

SOPHIA follows LOGOS's systematic list format for the allegorical assignments, which most clearly communicates the parable's structure.

---

## Similitude 5, Part 5 — The Allegorical Key

**59:1** I asked him further to explain all the parables and visions I had seen. He said to me: "In all the matters I am about to show you, I will provide explanation. Only give me your complete attention of heart and mind, and everything I tell you will be clarified."

**59:2** "The field is this world. The lord of the field is the one who created all things, brought them to completion, and empowered them. The son is the Holy Spirit. The slave is the Son of God. The vine is the people whom he planted. The fences are the holy angels of the Lord who keep his people. The weeds pulled from the vineyard are the transgressions of the servants of God. The foods sent from the feast are the commandments that he gave to his people through his Son. The friends and counselors are the holy angels who were created first. And the absence of the master is the time remaining before his coming."

**59:3** I said to him: "Lord, all these things are great and marvelous and glorious. Could I have perceived them by myself?" He said to me: "No one who has God in his heart would have hesitated to ask, nor would he have failed to receive the explanation. But I will speak with you."

**59:4** "Hear now. The slave whom the master approved and made the principal heir of all his goods — that is the Son of God. The counselors are the first-created angels. The absence of the master denotes the time remaining before his coming. The vine that is cultivated is the people of God. The fences are the angels who guard the people. The weeds pulled out are the sins of the servants. The foods sent from the feast are the commandments given to the people through the Son. The friends are the holy prophets who served God."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
